clue.text: Peers' dress under street lights

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed under another comes after it

parts.note: peers of the realm wear ceremonial robes in the House of Lords

explanation.surface: Members of the House of Lords parade in their finery beneath the street lamps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peers' here are members of the House of Lords, not equals or people looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Strobes are flashing lamps, a kind of light used in clubs and photography.

clue.text: Creature with no lead makes a point

indicators.note: losing its lead means the word for the creature drops its opening letter

parts.note: a beast is any animal or creature

explanation.surface: An animal let off its leash proves something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' just links the wordplay to 'a point', which is a compass point here, not an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the four cardinal points of the compass.

clue.text: Shows a response concerning laws

parts.note: RE is a Latin-derived word for concerning or about

explanation.surface: Someone responds to a matter about legislation.
explanation.definitionFit: To react is to respond to something, so this is a direct synonym in the third person.

clue.text: Part of London where men do not change

indicators.note: change tells us the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A district of the capital where the menfolk never alter their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do not change' reads as a refusal, but 'change' is the anagram signal working on MEN DO NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmonton is a district in the north London borough of Enfield.

clue.text: Insensitive rows on the radio — idiots!

indicators.note: something heard on the radio is only spoken, so a word that sounds the same is wanted

parts.note: to scull is to row a boat with oars

explanation.surface: A broadcaster scolds stupid people over unfeeling arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' looks like quarrels, but it is the verb, rowing a boat: SCULLS, which is said like SKULLS.
explanation.definitionFit: A numbskull is a slow-witted person, a dunce or fool.

clue.text: Instrument from old estate, say, indicator not actually starting

parts.note: an estate is a type of car, the say marking it as an example

indicators.note: starting means only the opening letter of each of these three words is used

explanation.surface: A musical instrument found on an old country estate, its pointer not truly beginning to move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'estate, say' is a car (an estate car is what Americans call a station wagon), not land.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes.

clue.text: Coming from the East, sailor is absorbed in marine books

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means reading right to left
being absorbed in means sitting inside the other piece

parts.note: the sea is the marine realm
an old salt is an experienced sailor

explanation.surface: An eastern seaman engrossed in naval reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marine' looks like a soldier but is the sea; 'is absorbed in' and 'Coming from the East' then build SESALTA and read it right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlases are books of maps.

clue.text: A record spinner with a French court auxiliary

parts.note: a DJ, or disc jockey, spins records

explanation.surface: A disc jockey with a French tennis court helper.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjunct is an extra, supporting thing, so auxiliary is a close synonym.

clue.text: Summit cost includes new heir

parts.note: the crown of a hill is its top or summit

indicators.note: includes means the cost word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: price is a synonym of cost

explanation.surface: The expense of a summit meeting takes in a new successor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summit' suggests a political meeting, but here it is a hilltop, the crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A crown prince is the male heir to a throne.

clue.text: Serve cornmeal to the rich and famous seen here

definitions.text: the rich and famous seen here

indicators.note: serving food means preparing it, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Offering polenta to celebrities in a glamorous resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' looks like a link word but is part of the anagram: CORNMEAL TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Monte Carlo in Monaco is a resort famous for its casino and wealthy visitors.

clue.text: Having nothing on except for start of exams

parts.note: bar means except, as in all bar one

indicators.note: start of means take just the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A student who wears nothing but for the first day of exams.
explanation.definitionFit: Bare means naked, with no clothes on.

clue.text: One wants to change something for a carpenter

indicators.note: the wish to change suggests the letters of the two words are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone longs for a different tool in the woodwork shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon saw is a fine-toothed saw that woodworkers use for joints.

clue.text: Sunblock that's nearly ooze when spread

indicators.note: spreading something rearranges it, so the preceding letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A sun cream that almost oozes when rubbed on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' tempts a solver to cut a letter from ooze; it is anagram fodder in full.
explanation.definitionFit: The ozone layer in the upper atmosphere screens out much of the sun's ultraviolet light, a witty sunblock.

clue.text: Accepting family should wear label

indicators.note: wearing something puts it on, so the label wraps round the family word

explanation.surface: Relatives ought to put on name badges.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking is accepting something offered, as in taking a gift.

clue.text: A loser plans different devices to produce energy

indicators.note: different means the letters are made into something else by rearranging

explanation.surface: A failed inventor dreams up new power generators.
explanation.definitionFit: Solar panels turn sunlight into electricity, so they are energy-producing devices.

clue.text: A disease might be thus carried by music

indicators.note: carried by music places the carried word after the music word

parts.note: an air is a tune or piece of music

explanation.surface: An illness spread through song.
explanation.definitionFit: An airborne disease is one transmitted through the air, as many infections are.

clue.text: Steam cleaned or sent back for an expert

indicators.note: cleaning something out turns it over, so the letters of steam are reordered
sent back means the little word is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A steam-cleaned item or one returned to a specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleaned' turns STEAM into MAEST, and 'sent back' reverses OR to RO.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a master or distinguished expert, especially in music.

clue.text: The sort of language used in court?

definitions.text: The sort of language used in court?

parts.words: The sort of language used in court?
parts.note: court seems to be a law court, but it is courting: the words of wooing, and also the family of Latin-derived tongues

explanation.definitionFit: Romance is the wooing talk of courtship and the family of Latin-descended languages such as French.

clue.text: Calling for run?

definitions.meaning: a calling is a vocation or profession
to run fast and out of control, to hurtle

explanation.surface: Shouting for someone to dash.
explanation.definitionFit: A career is one's profession, and to career is to rush headlong.

clue.text: One seeking return from popular voters being reselected

indicators.note: reselecting shuffles the choice, so the letters of voters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician hoping to come back from electors who are choosing again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' seems electoral, but it is a profit on money put in.
explanation.definitionFit: An investor puts money in hoping for a return on it.

clue.text: The foresight to call round, lacking time before working

indicators.note: placed before means the first piece comes ahead of the next
lacking means the following letter is removed

parts.note: to call round is to visit someone

explanation.surface: Someone foresighted pops over, but has no time before work.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision means foresight, imagination about the future.

clue.text: Part of planet motorists accept is going backwards

indicators.note: accepting something means holding it inside

parts.note: the AA, the Automobile Association, is Britain's motorists' organisation

indicators.note: going backwards means the little word is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Drivers admit they are reversing round part of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is the UK's Automobile Association, a breakdown service for drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a continent, a large part of the planet.

clue.text: So conical a shape must be infrequent

indicators.note: shaping something remoulds it, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A cone shape like this has to be rare.
explanation.definitionFit: Occasional means happening now and then, not often.

clue.text: Nothing demanded outside ultimately diminishes chances

indicators.note: outside means take just the outer letters of the word
ultimately points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A demand made outdoors that eventually reduces the prospects.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds are the chances or likelihood of something happening.

clue.text: Running away to change sides is liberating

indicators.note: changing sides swaps left for right, so L becomes R

explanation.surface: A defector running off to the other side finds it freeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change sides' looks like defection; it swaps L (left) for R (right) in FLEEING.
explanation.definitionFit: Freeing means releasing or liberating.

clue.text: Transmit direct

definitions.meaning: to pass heat or electricity through, as a wire does
to lead an orchestra or manage an activity

explanation.definitionFit: Conduct means both carrying electricity or heat and leading or managing something.
